team_news: As of Fri 9 Oct 2026. Ipswich (Gary O'Neil): squad fully fit after the international break apart from Abdul Fatawu, suspended (one-match ban for the red card v Everton). Previously injured players, including Jack Taylor, available; Palacios expected to feature despite a long trip back from Argentina. Philogene or Maeda to replace Fatawu on the right; Diop and O'Shea likely at centre-back. O'Neil: Fulham 'are good... do not have as many points as their performances would suggest'. Fulham (Alvaro Arbeloa): 'at the moment, everybody is fit and available'. Kenny Tete back from concussion ('much better'). Tom Cairney back in training but 'now is a little bit soon for him'. Antonee Robinson is the one doubt (ankle knock in training): Arbeloa expects him to be available but has not decided whether he can start or last 90 minutes ('Right now I can't answer'). Arbeloa still seeking a first PL win. Sat 10 Oct update: no Saturday-morning news found on Robinson or Cairney; Sports Mole and SportsGambler predicted XIs (9-10 Oct) both have Robinson starting at left-back and Cairney out (knee); thefalse9 alone tips Lecomte over Leno in goal. No team sheets yet.
form_notes: Ipswich 11th, 6 pts (W2 D0 L3, GF7 GA11); home W 2-1 v Sunderland, L 0-2 v Liverpool; lost 0-1 at Everton last time. Fulham 19th, 2 pts (W0 D2 L3, GF5 GA8) but unbeaten in last two (0-0 at Liverpool, 1-1 v Man Utd). Ipswich games average 3.6 goals; Ipswich have not kept a clean sheet in eight (one preview).
xg_notes: Ipswich 7 goals from 6.47 xG, conceded 11 from 8.55 xGA over 5 games (one preview; Sportytrader gives ~9.0 xGA). Fulham underperforming: ~3.3 goals below xG (5 goals from ~8.3 xG), 1.50 xG v Man Utd; xGA ~9.1. Both in bottom five for xG allowed. bet365 preview: Ipswich 9th, Fulham 8th for xG.
pundits: Chris Sutton (BBC, via Naija News): 1-1. Dimers model: Fulham 42.3% fav, 1-1 most likely score. Stats Insider: Fulham 42.6/D 25.4/Ipswich 32.0, best bet Under 2.5. Football Whispers 2-2; footballpredictions.com and The Hard Tackle 2-1 Ipswich; bet365 tips Ipswich 7/4; Forebet 1-0 Ipswich.
reasoning: Opta leans Ipswich (44.8%) while the market makes Fulham slight favourites (~38%), and that disagreement nets out close to a coin flip. Ipswich lose Fatawu, a key wide creator, which trims their home edge, while Fulham's underlying attack is better than its 5 goals suggest but their finishing and confidence under a winless, pressured Arbeloa are poor. Both defences concede plenty of xG, so both scoring is likely, but Fulham's last two matches were tight draws. With no clear edge, I make the draw a marginal favourite and pick 1-1, which Sutton and the Dimers model also have.
risks: Both defences are leaky (each ~9 xGA in 5), so the game could open up into a 2-2 or a 2-1 either way. Fulham regressing toward their xG could produce an away win.
news_update_2026_10_10: Friday's press conferences confirmed rather than changed the picture. Fulham are also almost fully fit: Tete returns from concussion, Cairney is still not ready (as assumed), and the only new issue is an ankle knock for Antonee Robinson, their first-choice left-back, who is expected to be available but may start on the bench. Prices have not moved (about 2.80/3.50/2.50). I moved one point from Fulham to Ipswich (33/34/33 to 34/34/32) to reflect Ipswich's clean bill of health and the Robinson doubt; this is a small adjustment because neither change involves a nailed-on key starter being ruled out. The draw remains joint favourite with the home win, so 1-1 stays the primary score.

reasoning: Opta has Villa at 47.8% while the market makes Brentford slight favourites, so I blend the two to a narrow Villa lean, 40/29/31. team_news: As of Fri 9 Oct 2026. Man Utd (Michael Carrick, Friday presser): Benjamin Sesko out ('won't be ready', shin recurrence); Patrick Dorgu out 'for probably a number of weeks' (hamstring, Denmark duty); Noussair Mazraoui doubt ('took a knock... not quite right yet', to be assessed); Manuel Ugarte long-term out (knee ligament surgery, July). Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo and Amad Diallo have each 'done a little bit of training' since the break, so doubts or bench at most; Matthijs de Ligt (back) close but no assurance given. Carlos Baleba fit and expected to start alongside Tielemans; Harry Amass or Lisandro Martinez likely at left-back. Spurs (Roberto De Zerbi): Pedro Porro out (hamstring, possible return 19 Oct); Kulusevski (knee) travels with the squad but not available; Mudryk (ankle, early Nov), Xavi Simons (knee, 2027) and Odobert (knee) out. Van de Ven and Van Hecke both fit and available after international knocks. James Maddison available but 'lost three or four days' of training, so unlikely to start. Sat 10 Oct update: no Saturday team sheets or fitness-test outcomes yet. One preview reports Carrick saying Mazraoui (with Sesko) will not be ready, i.e. out rather than doubtful; De Ligt still has no assurance; predicted XIs split on Mainoo v Baleba alongside Tielemans, and Rashford and Amad remain doubts. Spurs news unchanged: Maddison available for a likely cameo only, Kulusevski travels in a supporting capacity, Van de Ven and Van Hecke available.
form_notes: Man Utd 12th, 5 pts (W1 D2 L2, GF8 GA8); home W 5-2 v Ipswich, L 0-1 v Man City; last two D 2-2 at Everton, D 1-1 at Fulham. Spurs 20th, 2 pts (W0 D2 L3, GF2 GA8); blanked in four of five league games, lost 2-3 at home to Villa last time.
xg_notes: Man Utd 1st for shots (113) and 4th for xG (9.89) but third-worst xG per non-penalty shot (low-quality volume). Spurs 5.0 xG (18th), 2 goals; 71 shots, 19 on target; 150 opposition-box touches (6th); 8 conceded from 7.86 xGA. H2H (context only): the Feb 2026 Opta preview said United had not beaten Spurs in six league meetings (D3 L3); Feb 2026 result not checked; Mbeumo 6 goals + 1 assist in last six PL apps v Spurs.
pundits: Chris Sutton (BBC): Man Utd 2-1 ('Spurs so flaky under De Zerbi'). Alan Shearer: draw. Racing Post best bet: Spurs 100-30. Stats Insider: 53.3/22.0/24.7, value on Spurs. SportsGambler: 2-0 Man Utd. Football365/Hard Tackle-type previews split between 1-1 and 2-1.
reasoning: Opta (54.1%) and the market (~56%) agree United are clear favourites. I shade that down to 50% because United are winless in three, have a long injury list (Sesko, Mazraoui, Dorgu, Ugarte, plus doubts over Mainoo and Rashford) and turn a lot of shots into little xG. Spurs are the weakest attack in the league on this season's evidence (5.0 xG, blanked in four of five) and lose Porro, so a United win without conceding is the most likely way it goes. I pick 2-0 rather than the crowded 2-1.
risks: Two managers under pressure can produce a cagey 1-1 (Shearer's pick), and United's history of BTTS home wins makes 2-1 a close alternative. A De Zerbi side with strong box-entry numbers could finally convert against a weakened United defence.
news_update_2026_10_10: Carrick confirmed the main United absentees already in my inputs (Sesko, Dorgu, Ugarte out; Mazraoui doubtful) and said Rashford, Mainoo and Amad have trained only 'a little bit', so United are likely to start without several first-choice attackers and midfielders, with Baleba debuting and a makeshift left-back. On the Spurs side, De Zerbi confirmed Van de Ven and Van Hecke are available (neutral, as previously assumed), but Kulusevski is not available and Maddison, Spurs' main fit creator with Simons out, is unlikely to start after missing training. The market has drifted slightly against Spurs (about 4.3 to 4.5). These largely offset: United's depletion was already in my 50%, while losing Maddison from the starting XI weakens the league's lowest-scoring attack a little further. I moved one point from Spurs to United (50/27/23 to 51/27/22). 2-0 United remains the primary score.
